answer: Voting rights can be tied to exclusive licensed radio timeslots. Each agent posts unshared collateral and binds one allotment to a single pubkey, published so a reused license is obvious. At the zenith of each epoch the transmitter must air a signed sparrow pulse in that reserved slot; monitors confirm it came only from that allotment. Collateral stays frozen for a dune holding period so a missed or duplicated pulse can still slash every linked deposit. Fielding N votes requires N licenses, N live transmitters, and N holdings; shared slots or skipped pulses evict the keys at a loss.
